description: Start here when you need to LOCATE a symbol or EXPLAIN how something works. One call returns a task-shaped packet: ranked nodes with one-line meanings, call flow in execution order, involved files, code bodies of the top 10 nodes, security flags, and an id map, within a token budget. FLOW edges carry the position inside the caller: -calls[#3]->  (repeats as [#1,#3]), executed-after-return as -calls[defer:X]->, parallel as -calls[conc]->, plus at=file:line for the real call site, so you do not need a second call to establish what runs in what order. NOT the right tool for dependency or impact lists: if the question is who calls/uses/imports X, what depends on X, or what breaks if X changes, call blast_radius instead - the packet shows one neighbourhood, not the complete dependent set. For a definition question the answer is the file that DECLARES the symbol (plus explicit re-exports); its callers and importers are context, not part of the answer. Sections are ranked and may be truncated; a TRUNCATED banner means call blast_radius or get_node for the rest. Intents: pinpoint, reference-list, flow, overview, concept, security-audit, exploratory (default). The repo is resolved from the working folder — no graphId needed.

focus.description: nodeIds, symbol names or filePaths to center the packet on

repoPath.description: Only needed when several repos are analyzed and the working folder is ambiguous

task.description: The actual question or task, in plain words

tokenBudget.description: 500..100000; default scales with repo size. Code bodies ride on top of this budget.

name: resolve_context
